# Fork-maintained patches for rayward-external/litellm
#
# Upstream (BerriAI/litellm) uses ARG-variable FROM in Dockerfiles.
# Our fork pins literal image@sha256 digests so Scorecard/OpenSSF does not flag them.
# Upstream syncs may revert to ARG-only FROM; daily-patch-verify detects and re-pins.
#
# Format: <file> | <grep_pattern_that_proves_patch_is_present> | <human_description>

Dockerfile            | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM); this is the Dockerfile litellm-build-push.yml deploys (Scorecard PinnedDependenciesID)
backend/Dockerfile    | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
gateway/Dockerfile    | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
migrations/Dockerfile | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
.github/workflows/codeql.yml        | timeout-minutes: 90                       | CodeQL analyze job timeout raised 30->90 min so python leg completes
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/log-injection                          | Exclude CWE-117 query: taint explosion from pervasive logging; same scaling class as py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | workflow_dispatch                          | Alert bridge for code-scanning triage; re-apply after -X theirs syncs that wipe .github/workflows/
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24         | Opt in to Node.js 24 runtime before GitHub's 2026-06-16 forced migration (upload-artifact@v4 is a Node 20 action)
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | list_secrets                               | mode=list_secrets: reads secret-scanning/alerts through the same security-events:write token scope, since the security-sweep's CCR token cannot call that API directly. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once the CCR/Claude GitHub App token gains secret-scanning-alert read scope directly.
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | REF_FILTER                                 | Optional `ref` input for mode=list. GitHub's /code-scanning/alerts endpoint without a ref filter does not surface alerts scoped only to a PR head/merge ref (found on 2026-08-04 triaging PR #182: the unfiltered list said 0 open alerts while the PR's own CodeQL check reported 1 new high alert); passing ref=refs/pull/<n>/merge (or refs/heads/<branch>) surfaces those. Also added per-alert file:line output to the list mode's step summary.
cookbook/livekit_agent_sdk/requirements.txt | json-repair>=0.60.1                  | Explicit pin forcing the livekit-agents[xai] transitive json-repair dependency past GHSA-xf7x-x43h-rpqh (unbounded CPU DoS via circular JSON-schema $ref). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once livekit-agents itself requires json-repair>=0.60.1.
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | cookbook                                   | paths-ignore: cookbook/ and scripts/benchmark_* are example/benchmark code; excluded to prevent FP CodeQL alerts (py/reflective-xss #953, py/regex-injection #952, py/clear-text-storage #979 #980)
litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py   | re\.escape\(allowed_model_pattern\)        | is_model_allowed_by_pattern: re.escape() the wildcard pattern before building the match regex, closing py/regex-injection (#1024). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream applies the same escape fix.
litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/litellm_content_filter/content_filter.py | resolved category file path escapes categories_dir | _load_categories: realpath/commonpath containment re-check on category_file_path immediately before use, closing py/path-injection (#1025) as defense-in-depth alongside the existing category_name regex validation. CodeQL (PR #182) flagged this same rule again on 2026-08-04: the containment check validated real_category_file_path but the subsequent os.path.exists()/_load_category_file() sinks still read the unsanitized category_file_path, so the taint path through the un-normalized variable was never actually closed. Both sinks now take real_category_file_path. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream applies an equivalent containment check.
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/stack-trace-exposure                    | Exclude CWE-209 query: tracebacks only reach loggers, ProxyException.to_dict() never serializes a traceback field, CodeQL cannot distinguish log sinks from HTTP response sinks
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization   | Exclude CWE-184 query: security-critical URL validation uses urlparse() tuple comparison; flagged startswith/endswith are non-security normalization (JWT heuristic, trailing-slash strip)
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/request-without-cert-validation          | Exclude CWE-295 query: every httpx client resolves verify via get_ssl_verify()/get_ssl_configuration() (litellm/llms/custom_httpx/http_handler.py), defaulting to True and only disabled via explicit operator opt-in (SSL_VERIFY env var / litellm.ssl_verify / explicit param) for enterprise self-signed/internal-CA deployments; CodeQL cannot follow the dynamic default so it flags every call site

.github/dependabot.yml | package-ecosystem: "uv" | Fork-only dependabot config covering every ecosystem the fork's security sweep scans (github-actions, uv, pip for cookbook, npm for all 4 lockfile dirs, cargo for litellm-rust, gomod for terraform/provider and cookbook/gollem_go_agent_framework, docker for both Dockerfile locations); upstream has none. A 2026-07-25 security sweep found a second .github/dependabot.yaml file (added by an earlier sweep, commit 4ce563ba/#109) had silently split off the github-actions/docker ecosystems and the then-existing uv langchain ignore into a file GitHub does not read when dependabot.yml also exists — Dependabot was only ever running the entries in this .yml file, so those ecosystems and the ignore rule were dead since #109. Merged everything from the .yaml file into this one and deleted it. The langchain ignore itself was removed by the 2026-08-01 security sweep once the fork's pyproject.toml pins (langchain==1.3.9, langgraph>=1.2.4,<1.3.0) already satisfied the constraint the ignore was blocking Dependabot from proposing — leaving it in place would have suppressed every future langchain security bump, not just the resolved one. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove/merge if upstream ever ships its own dependabot.yml that a sync would otherwise clobber.

litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py | Applied across all keys for this team\.\n    Example - update team TPM Limit | update_team's docstring documents mcp_rpm_limit (wording copied verbatim from new_team's existing line). UpdateTeamRequest gained the mcp_rpm_limit field upstream but update_team's docstring was never updated, so tests/documentation_tests/test_api_docs.py fails: it diffs a function's docstring against its request model's model_fields. Both the endpoint and the model are IDENTICAL to upstream, so this is upstream breakage, not a fork artifact — upstream's own CI misses it. NOTE the grep pattern is deliberately anchored on the following "Example - update team TPM Limit" line: new_team carries the same sentence, so matching the sentence alone would report this patch present even after a sync drops it. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream documents mcp_rpm_limit in update_team's docstring itself.

Every -X theirs sync so far has silently dropped this (restored three times now: commit 343d3008, the 2026-07-12 sync, and the 2026-07-16 sync); it never conflicts textually with upstream's edits to the surrounding transform_request body, so git's 3-way merge just drops it instead of flagging a conflict. Signatures must be re-checked against upstream's current _is_adaptive_thinking_model/_validate_effort_for_model signatures each time (upstream has added a custom_llm_provider parameter to both since this was first written) — do not copy-paste the old diff verbatim. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream ships equivalent legacy-thinking-to-adaptive translation itself.

The repo's own budget-ratchet job (test-linting.yml) is explicitly documented as non-gating and exists precisely to surface a ceiling raise like this one as a review signal. litellm/utils.py | def _client_side_bad_request | Pre-flight request validators (validate_chat_completion_user_messages, validate_chat_completion_tool_choice) raise litellm.BadRequestError instead of a bare Exception. These run in completion() BEFORE a deployment is picked, so a bare Exception could not be mapped by exception_type() and fell through to APIConnectionError: callers got HTTP 500 attributed to whichever provider the router was about to try -- a provider that never saw the request -- and _should_retry(500) then retried a permanently-invalid payload. Diagnosed 2026-07-21 from a live report where a client posted content-part dicts with no "type" key and spent a session chasing a Baseten outage that never happened. model/llm_provider are deliberately empty so no false attribution is reintroduced. Covered by tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py::test_validate_chat_completion_user_messages_raises_bad_request and ::test_validation_bad_request_is_not_remapped_to_api_connection_error (that path, NOT tests/litellm_utils_tests/, is the tree the test-unit `misc` job actually runs). REMOVAL CONDITION: fork-permanent for now. Do NOT open an upstream PR to carry this without the repo owner explicitly asking for one; remove only if upstream ships an equivalent fix on its own.
CLAUDE.md | RAYWARD FORK ONLY | Fork-only "PRs go to THIS fork, never upstream" section pinned at the top of upstream's CLAUDE.md. Both this file and AGENTS.md are SHARED with upstream, so a -X theirs sync silently drops the section and the next agent reads a file that says nothing about PR targets — which is exactly how an unauthorized PR got opened against BerriAI/litellm on 2026-07-21 (closed, branch deleted). REMOVAL CONDITION: none; this is a standing org policy, not a temporary divergence.
AGENTS.md | rayward-external/litellm` only | Fork-only PR-target rule appended to upstream's AGENTS.md, pointing at the CLAUDE.md section above. Same shared-with-upstream drop risk. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; standing org policy.

litellm/types/interactions/generated.py | queued = "queued" | Adds the `queued` member to BOTH Interaction status enums (Status1 lowercase, Status3 uppercase). The file is datamodel-codegen output from https://ai.google.dev/static/api/interactions.openapi.json pinned at 2025-12-16; Google has since added a `queued` status, so the generated enums are stale and a real `status: "queued"` response would fail Pydantic validation at runtime. Added by hand rather than regenerating, to avoid pulling unrelated spec drift into a validation-fix PR — a full datamodel-codegen refresh is worth doing separately. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream regenerates this file against a spec that already includes `queued`.

It fired correctly; the review outcome is the generated.py fix above. litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py | from litellm.router_strategy.tag_based_routing import | Fork-only hard-provider-pin (P1) + attribution-tag-sanitize (P2) hardening uses PINNED_PROVIDER_ROUTE_KEY, ORIGINAL_REQUEST_TAGS_KEY, ORIGINAL_REQUEST_TAGS_SNAPSHOT_TAKEN_KEY and PIN_TAG_PREFIX from litellm/router_strategy/tag_based_routing.py to strip client-supplied route-pin/tag-snapshot signals from request metadata and re-assert only the trusted request.state-derived pin. The 2026-07-22 -X theirs sync dropped only this import line (the surrounding import block textually conflicted with upstream's own edits, so git's 3-way merge silently resolved without flagging a conflict), leaving all 4 names undefined at module import time — broke every proxy test job's conftest import. litellm-rust/crates/core/Cargo.toml | aws-sdk-sts.*default-https-client | aws-sdk-sts's own "rustls" feature name is misleading: it maps to aws-smithy-runtime's legacy "tls-rustls" feature (hyper 0.14 + rustls 0.21.12 + rustls-webpki 0.101.7), not the modern stack. That legacy webpki was vulnerable to RUSTSEC-2026-0098/0099/0104 (name-constraint bypass and a reachable panic in certificate parsing). Switched the feature request to "default-https-client", which resolves to the same modern rustls-aws-lc/webpki-0.103+ stack that aws-config's own "rustls" feature already uses (aws-config's "rustls" = "client-hyper" = "default-https-client"; only aws-sdk-sts's naming was inconsistent). No code in this workspace references the legacy hyper-0.14 connector directly, so the swap is drop-in. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream smithy-rs renames aws-sdk-sts's "rustls" feature to resolve to the modern stack, matching aws-config, itself.

litellm/proxy/common_utils/budget_window_headers.py | def format_budget_windows | feature (#481, reshaped #491): renders a key's CONCURRENT budget windows (1d/1w/1mo) into x-usage-budget. Broker keys set `budget_limits`, never top-level `max_budget`, so get_custom_headers read None -> "None" -> dropped by exclude_values, and the header NEVER shipped to an external caller. Carries `spent` alongside `limit` per window because x-usage-spend is LIFETIME and cannot be subtracted from a windowed cap (a fourth header was declined, owner 2026-08-02). #491 MOVED THE HEADER NAME: BUDGET_HEADER_NAME is now the fork-only `x-litellm-key-budget-windows`, NOT upstream's `x-litellm-key-max-budget`. Overloading the upstream name put two value types under it, which no reader can dispatch on — the fork's own gateway_cost.py did float(raw) and silently reported max_budget:None for every windowed key. NEUTRAL_BUDGET_HEADER_NAME ("x-usage-budget") is exported beside it so the guards can assert both halves. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop if upstream ever publishes per-window budgets itself. #491 FOLLOW-UP: format_budget_windows also COLLAPSES same-duration windows to the least-remaining one. The published format is a list keyed by window name and the customer-facing parser turns it into a dict, so two entries sharing a duration silently overwrite each other — and the later assignment wins, so the LOOSER cap survives and headroom is overstated. The sibling gateway shipped exactly this (1d;limit=1000 beside 1d;limit=5000 reported $4999.89 of headroom against a real $999.99 cap). Duplicates are not configured here today, but budget_limits is an iterated LIST not a mapping, so it is one config edit away. Do not simplify this back to a plain join.
litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py | valid_token.budget_window_usage | feature (#481) — THE SOURCE. _virtual_key_multi_budget_check already reads every window's counter (it is the enforcement); this stashes what it read so the sync get_custom_headers can publish it without a second cache round-trip and without disagreeing with the numbers enforcement acted on. Losing this line leaves the formatter correct and the header empty — silent.
litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py | format_budget_windows(getattr | feature (#481, extended #491) — THE WIRING, tracked separately because losing it is silent and the formatter's own tests stay green. There are now TWO format_budget_windows call sites and they are not interchangeable: one fills the NEUTRAL `x-usage-budget` (for internal callers — the external allowlist drops it by design), the other fills the fork-only branded twin `x-litellm-key-budget-windows` that the external rename table reads. Losing either silently blinds exactly one audience. The same patch emits `x-usage-cost` / `x-usage-spend` at source so the documented contract works on the internal hostname too, and RESTORES upstream's `"x-litellm-key-max-budget": str(user_api_key_dict.max_budget)` — do not re-add the `or str(...)` overload a sync may suggest. NOTE the getattr: direct attribute access would raise AttributeError on EVERY request if the _types.py half is reverted by a sync, and breaks upstream tests that build MagicMock(spec=UserAPIKeyAuth) since pydantic v2 fields are invisible to a mock spec. Both were observed 2026-08-02. The wiring guards assert over the AST, not source text, because ruff format reflows these calls.
litellm/proxy/_types.py | budget_window_usage | feature (#481): transient per-request field on UserAPIKeyAuth holding the window snapshot, exclude=True like the neighbouring budget_reservation — never persisted, never part of the key's API shape.
litellm/proxy/middleware/external_audience_middleware.py | RENAMED_HEADERS | security (#441/#443/#487, retuned #491) — the ENTIRE external-audience response policy, and it had no manifest entry until #491. A strict ALLOWLIST plus a three-entry rename table; losing it exposes x-litellm-* (names our gateway software), llm_provider-* (proves we proxy, carries upstream request ids) and bare x-ratelimit-* (OUR purchased quota) to external parties. THE RENAME IS THE ONLY WAY A NEUTRAL NAME REACHES AN EXTERNAL CALLER and that is load-bearing, not tidiable: the neutral names are deliberately absent from ALLOWED_HEADERS so a source-emitted copy (#491 emits all three internally) and a hostile upstream copy on the pass-through path both die at the boundary, leaving exactly one value. Allowlisting any neutral name forfeits that. The budget entry reads the fork-only `x-litellm-key-budget-windows`, never upstream's `x-litellm-key-max-budget` — renaming the latter would publish `None` for every windowed key. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; this is ours permanently.
litellm/constants.py | "x-usage-cost", | feature (#491): appends the three neutral usage names to LITELLM_UI_ALLOW_HEADERS, which proxy_server.py passes to CORSMiddleware as expose_headers. Emitting a response header is NOT enough for a cross-origin browser caller — a browser returns null from response.headers for any name absent from that list, with no error raised, so the loss is silent. Internal callers only; the external middleware REPLACES access-control-expose-headers with the neutral names because this list advertises literal x-litellm-* names and is itself a disclosure. Found by review, not by a test: the suite drives the app in-process where CORS never runs. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop if upstream ever exposes these itself.

Until then this line stays as an open flag, not a closed patch.

The fork's continuation-prompt retry branch in `_acompletion_streaming_iterator`/`_completion_streaming_iterator` is now unreachable by construction and was deleted rather than left dead -- this sync's own new test asserts the router "must re-raise instead of attempting a continuation-prompt fallback, because partial content has already been sent to the client"; the Responses-API iterator's own continuation-prompt injection is untouched (a separate test asserts it still happens). All 174 tests in test_router.py pass. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; this supersedes router.py's entry in the line above -- treat router.py as fully reconciled, not deferred. If any of the OTHER 11 files in that round-1 restore turn out to have the same test-breaking pattern (a new upstream helper/behavior their own test suite expects), redo them the same way rather than assuming a wholesale restore was safe there either.

2026-08-05 sync merge corruption, round 3 (CI-red gaps missed by the round-1 12-file list) | litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py: `initialize_pinned_provider_routes` | Two more silent drops from the same -X theirs sync, found only because CI's proxy-infra job stayed red after the round-1/round-2 fixes landed. (1) litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py: ProxyConfig.load_config's entire "provider-pinned standard routes" hook block (the app.state prior-registration probe, the assert_tag_filtering_enabled_for_pinned_routes boot guard, and the initialize_pinned_provider_routes call) was dropped outright -- the merge conflated this fork-only block with upstream's neighboring `Final`-annotation edits to the same region (`router_params`, `model_list`, etc., the same 2708620d-crossing pattern as the round-1 12) and it fell out entirely, with zero import error since nothing outside load_config called it. This file was never in the round-1 12-file list because ruff F821/F401 saw nothing wrong. Restored the block verbatim from origin/litellm_internal_staging (pre-sync fork state) at its original call site, immediately after the litellm_license premium_user check and before router_params. (2) litellm/llms/cohere/common_utils.py: `CohereV2ModelResponseIterator._parse_message_end` reverted from the fork's dual-envelope read (`data = chunk.get("data"); delta = (data if isinstance(data, dict) else chunk).get("delta", {})`, PR-documented as fixing streamed Cohere passthrough usage always parsing as `None`) back to a wrapped-only read (`chunk.get("data", {}).get("delta", {})`) that never matches the real SSE shape (`{"type": "message-end", "delta": {...}}`, the same top-level shape `_parse_content_delta` reads) -- silently reintroducing the exact $0-streamed-cost bug the dual-envelope read was written to fix. This file also wasn't in the round-1 12 (Final-annotation-only diff elsewhere in the file masked the one real logic hunk). Restored the dual-envelope read and its explanatory docstring verbatim from origin/litellm_internal_staging. REMOVAL CONDITION: like the round-1/round-2 entries, these are regression fixes, not ongoing patches -- nothing to remove. Procedural lesson: the round-1 12-file list was derived from a single ruff F821/F401 sweep plus one manual audit, which is NOT a complete method for this failure class (dropped-block/dropped-logic-kept-callsite corruptions that produce no import error); a green ruff sweep after a -X theirs sync across 2708620d's history is not sufficient evidence that no file needs restoration -- CI failing tests were the only signal for both of these.

Procedural lesson: an F821/F401-clean tree after an -X theirs sync across 2708620d's history is still not sufficient; a full call-site (not just bare-name) audit or a green test run of every touched file is needed to catch a dropped-method-kept-callsite corruption.
